issues.description: The problem statement UML and the template code refer to an interface named 'Milkable' with the method signature String messageOnMilk(), but the solution repository defines an interface named 'Dairy' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Dairy.java) that provides String messageOnMilk(), and also contains an empty Milkable.java file. Goat and Seal in the solution implement Dairy rather than Milkable. This naming mismatch between the expected interface name (Milkable) and the solution's interface (Dairy), plus the presence of an empty Milkable.java, will confuse students and tools that look for the Milkable interface declared in the exercise description and template (for example the template Main uses Milkable[] milkables = new Milkable[]{goat, seal};).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the solution's 'Dairy' interface to 'Milkable' (package de.tum.cit.ase) and ensure it declares String messageOnMilk(); remove the empty Milkable.java file from the solution. Update Goat.java and Seal.java to implement Milkable instead of Dairy. Alternatively, if keeping 'Dairy' is desired, replace occurrences of 'Milkable' in the problem statement/template (and the example Main) with 'Dairy' and remove the empty Milkable.java — but ensure all three artifacts (problem, template, solution) use the same interface name and signature.
